$comment: The pinned upstream. `scripts/sync-upstream.sh` reads this file and nothing else, so a
release bump is a one-line edit here followed by `scripts/regenerate.sh`.
The source is the per-release `-sources.jar` on Google Maven, NOT a checkout of
github.com/androidx/androidx. Both carry the same `src/main`, but the sources jar is the
artifact of a RELEASE: it is ~1 MB rather than a 5 GB monorepo, it is addressed by the exact
version string the catalog already depends on, and `group-index.xml` beside it is a ready-made
release feed for `.github/workflows/upstream-sync.yml`. androidx-main carries no release tags
at all (`git ls-remote --tags` returns nothing), so a git checkout could only ever be pinned to
a commit sha, which is not the thing that 'updates when a release happens'.
Everything the jar carries that is not Kotlin source is dropped by `tools/sync.py`: R.java,
META-INF and the documentation markdown. Tests, samples, benchmarks and integration tests are
not in a sources jar to begin with, which is the second reason to prefer it.

$artifactsNotSynced.compose-navigation: Wraps androidx.navigation's Android NavHost. The ui-builder renders components, not navigation graphs, so it buys nothing on wasm and drags in a second expect/actual surface.
$artifactsNotSynced.compose-material: Superseded by material3 for the kit this repository reproduces.
$artifactsNotSynced.compose-ui-tooling: Android-only tooling; a wasm host has no ComposeViewAdapter.
